title: Non-Orthogonal Amplitude Amplification for Hybrid CV-DV Quantum Processors
authors: Jiyuan Liu, Joel Bierman, Yuan Liu
abstract: We introduce a non-orthogonal amplitude amplification (NOAA) method for hybrid continuous-variable- discrete-variable (CV-DV) quantum processors, where the available CV-assisted projector is not perfectly se- lective for the target state. We establish a bound on the achievable target-state fidelity, which is determined by the initial target-state amplitude and the selectivity of the accessible reflection operator. This bound limits the performance of NOAA in hybrid CV-DV systems. To mitigate this limitation, we propose using a squeezed CV ancilla to reduce the overlap between relevant CV states and a hybrid quantum signal processing (HQSP) filter to suppress errors arising from imperfect knowledge of the target eigenenergy. Numerical simulations show that, for small initial target-state amplitudes, our protocol achieves higher fidelity and efficiency than the repeat-until-success (RUS) method despite the presence of non-orthogonality. For large initial amplitudes, RUS is already efficient, and amplitude amplification provides little additional advantage.
summary: This paper introduces Non-Orthogonal Amplitude Amplification (NOAA) for quantum processors combining continuous and discrete variables. It addresses fidelity limitations arising from non-orthogonal state overlaps and energy measurement errors. By proposing a High-Quality Spectral Projector (HQSP) filter, the authors show that their method outperforms standard techniques like RUS, particularly for preparing states with small initial amplitudes.
main_problem: The paper addresses developing a Non-Orthogonal Amplitude Amplification (NOAA) method for hybrid Continuous Variable-Discrete Variable (CV-DV) quantum processors when the available projector is not perfectly selective for the target state.
main_result: The proposed protocol, utilizing a squeezed CV ancilla and a HQSP filter, achieves higher fidelity and efficiency than the Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) method for small initial target amplitudes, even in the presence of non-orthogonality.
method: The authors generalize Amplitude Amplification (AA) to the NOAA framework and mitigate performance degradation using a High-Quality Spectral Projector (HQSP) filter to suppress errors from imperfect state discrimination and energy mismatch.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a hybrid CV-DV quantum processor, combining continuous variables (oscillators) with discrete variables (qubits). The protocol relies on spectral-transformation oracles acting on this coupled system.
key_observables: Target-state fidelity ($	ext{F}_{	ext{NOAA}}$), success probability ($P_s$), and the degree of fidelity degradation due to state non-orthogonality or energy mismatch.
important_parameters: Initial target-state amplitude ($\psi_0$), squeezing parameter ($r$), and the degree of energy mismatch ($\delta\alpha_0$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation is that the CV-assisted reflection is non-selective due to non-orthogonal CV states associated with different DV eigenstates, and the target eigenenergy may only be known approximately.
figures_summary: The notes mention analyzing oscillator wavepackets and filter responses, showing how the HQSP filter keeps the target wavepacket within the passband, which is crucial for maintaining high fidelity.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of non-orthogonality in CV-DV systems, derives the fidelity bounds, and then proposes the HQSP-assisted NOAA protocol. It compares this protocol's performance against the standard Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) method across different regimes of initial amplitude.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles practical limitations (non-orthogonality, imperfect knowledge) in implementing quantum search algorithms on complex, hybrid quantum hardware architectures.
